title: Big banks drag after gloomy outlook
full_text:
A gloomy mortgage outlook hit the sharemarket on Monday, with falls in the major banks offsetting gains out of the mining sector.
The benchmark ASX 200 dragged 31 points, or 0.33 per cent, to 9232.60, while the broader All Ordinaries slipped 21.10 points, or 0.22 per cent, to 9424.00.
The dollar appreciated to buy 70.66 US cents.
Despite the market falling, seven of the 11 sectors finished in the green. Leading the falls were the major banks, which sank on Westpac’s results, as the financials sector dropped 2.27 per cent on its own.
The big four bank said economic conditions were weakening, as it flagged a 20 per cent drop in mortgage applications in its latest results.
Westpac shares slumped 5.88 per cent to $35.70, National Australia Bank dropped 2.39 per cent to $41.22, Commonwealth Bank dragged 2.10 per cent to $174.27 and ANZ gave up 1.70 per cent to $37.09.
Offsetting the falls from the banking sector was a bounce in healthcare and mining stocks.
Vaccines giant CSL shares rallied 1.72 per cent to $134.47, ResMed surged 4.23 per cent to $30.09 and Pro Medicus added 0.30 per cent to $176.61. BHP shares added 0.87 per cent to $63.52, Rio Tinto closed up 0.77 per cent to $179.05 and Fortescue slipped 0.17 per cent to $17.99.
